issue_context.title: flowschemas resource is currently skipped by TestApplyResetFields test.
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:
`flowschemas` resource is currently skipped by `TestApplyResetFields` test.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/apiserver/apply/reset_fields_test.go#L70-L74
```
var resetFieldsSkippedResources = map[string]struct{}{
	// TODO: flowschemas is flaking,
	// possible bug in the flowschemas controller.
	"flowschemas": {},
}
```

When it flakes, it fails with the following error
```
 reset_fields_test.go:288: expected conflict, got error <nil>
```

this is the test result:
```
--- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields (5.94s)
    --- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2,_Resource=flowschemas (0.05s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
    --- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1,_Resource=flowschemas (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1,_Resource=flowschemas (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
```


#### What you expected to happen:

We need to identify the root case of why it flakes and fix it. "flowschemas" being skipped means that we may not catch any errors related to field resetting when we add a new version of the API.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- remove "flowschemas" from `resetFieldsSkippedResources`
- go test -v -count=1 ./test/integration/apiserver/apply -run="TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io"

run multiple times to see the flake

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments: @tkashem is someone going to look at this one or you need help from the broader sig? (we saw this one during triage)
@fedebongio I have limited knowledge on how the test `TestApplyResetFields` works. Yes, i would appreciate some help from the broader sig.

Judging from the comment it sounds like whoever wrote that believed that the APF controller was interfering with the test (probably by writing back a status). The fix might be to disable that controller for that test.

Current understanding is as follows.  The annotations needed to guide strategic merge patch are missing from the Condition slice field in FlowSchemaStatus and in PriorityLevelConfigurationStatus.  The APF config-consuming controller was written, however, with the mistaken understanding that a strategic merge patch of Status with one Condition will only affect that member of the Condition slice.  The truth is that currently such a patch will replace the entire slice.  That is why FlowSchema fails TestApplyResetFields and is specifically excluded.

#107456 will change that controller to use server-side apply instead of strategic merge patch, so that indeed only the one intended member of the Condition slice is affected.

#107574 calls for adding the missing annotations in the API.  This is too disruptive to do to an existing version and so will have to be done as we create the next version of the API.

review_comments:
asking once per 10s sounds like it can unnecessary extend time to run this test.
Maybe switch to 1s?

because strategic merge patches are computed client-side, changing this breaks compatibility with clients built against 1.23 and earlier versions of the API types. This would have to be fixed on a version boundary (v1beta3 or v1)
also, what does the `retainKeys` bit do? I don't see that used on any other conditions lists that use the merge strategy

Yeah, I think we should drop retainKeys.

@liggitt, adding the patchStrategy means that new clients will start sending correct patches and old clients will continue to do the wrong thing, isn't that better than having all clients do the wrong thing? Also, the wrong thing is only the wrong thing if clients send partial conditions, which I don't know if it happens.

> adding the patchStrategy means that new clients will start sending correct patches and old clients will continue to do the wrong thing, isn't that better than having all clients do the wrong thing?

I don't think so. "correct" is in the eye of the beholder (the server). This change means new clients will send incorrect patches to old servers... they'll compute a merge patch, send only the changed condition, and the old server will discard all other conditions.

I think this has to be changed in an API version boundary

As the author of the only known client, let me point out that due to the astonishing lack of documentation, this client (the APF config-consuming controller) sends a strategic merge patch with just one Condition in the Status but expects that the result will only be a modification of that individual Condition; this is the bug #104842 .

Due to the stunning lack of documentation, I do not see how we can be sure any other client --- if any exists at all --- is written with the correct interpretation of the existing annotations.

BTW, I found `,retainKeys` in the example I looked at, Pod.

Of course, we certainly can not assume that all client authors are as confused as I was.  So, yes, we fix this later.

That means that for now, @tkashem proceed with your PR that changes the controller to use SSA (#107456).  In this here PR you can see what I suppose is the intended breathless style of composing the ApplyConfiguration.

I will do something about a PR that adds a currently-correct test of patching.

> As the author of the only known client ...

I was referring to the strategic merge patches that the `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch` package (used by things like kubectl and [other tools](https://cs.github.com/?scopeName=All+repos&scope=&q=strategicpatch.Create+-org%3Akubernetes+extension%3Ago+-path%3Avendor+-path%3Astaging+-path%3Atest)) would generate automatically from the linked API types
